questions.question:
Which one of the given responses would be a meaningful order of the following words?

1. Sowing

2. Tilling

3. Reaping

4. Weeding
questions.solution:
Tilling comes first in the order.

It is followed by Sowing.

Sowing is followed by Weeding.

Weeding is followed by Reaping.

The correct meaningful order is,

Tilling (2) → Sowing (1) → Weeding (4) → Reaping (3)

Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Moat, Chain pump, Dhekli & Rahat are

options.text: The traditional methods of spraying pesticides
The traditional methods of sowing seeds

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Traditional methods of irrigation__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Traditional methods of irrigation consist of chain pump, dhekli, Moat, Rahat.
 
• 
 Dhekli method

 
 
• In the Dhekli method, the ropes and containers were used to gain water from the well. It is a commonly used method.
 
• There is a bucket and a rock is connected to a wooden beam at either ends.
 
• When the farmer sink an empty bucket into the water, the bucket is fetched up due to the weight of the rock attached to the other end of a wooden beam.
 
 
 
• Chain pump:
 
 
• It has been used since ancient times, in various parts of Europe, China, and the middle-east.
 
• Two sizable wheels are joined by an unending chain to form this traditional chain pump.
 
• Half of the bottom wheel is submerged in the water.
 
• The attached buckets drop into the pool when the wheel is rotated, collecting water.
 
• The water from the buckets is then moved from the higher wheel to the pool as the chain then hoists them there.
 
 
 
• **Moat Method**
 
 
• It is a pully system of Irrigation. 
 
 
 
• 
 Rahat method.

 
 
• In the Rahat method, animals move and rotate the wheel, which results in drawing the water from the well.
 
• IThe Cattle is attached to a wheel.
 
• When the cattle does the movement, it rotates the wheel that has buckets connected to it. 
 
• This results in drawing water from the well.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Irrigation

 
 
• The agricultural practise of applying regulated amounts of water to land to help in crop production, as well as to develop landscape plants and lawns, where it may be known as watering, is known as irrigation.
 
 
 
• Modern methods of irrigations includes Drip system and Sprinkler system.
 
 
• Sprinkler system:
 
 
• Pipes are used to spray water onto the fields in the form of rain-like water droplets.
 
• The sprinkler system prevents any water loss.
 
• This system does not have the waterlogging issue.
 
 
 
• Drip system: 
 
 
• ​The fields are covered in small pipes with tiny perforations.
 
• Water drips at the plant roots when it passes through pipes and is used for irrigation.
 
• The plants are supplied with water by the roots, which also absorb it.

Which of the following nutrients is provided to plants by fertilizers?

1. Nitrogen

2. Phosphorus

3. Potassium

Select the correct code.
questions.solution:
__Explanation__ 

__
 
• Fertilisers are chemical substances that are rich in a particular nutrient.
 
• Fertilisers are very rich in plant nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus & potassium.
 
• Some examples of fertilisers are— urea, ammonium sulphate, superphosphate, potash, NPK (Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium).
 
• They are used to ensure good vegetative growth (leaves, branches and flowers), giving rise to healthy plants.
 
• The use of fertilisers leads to a better yield of crops such as wheat, paddy and maize. But excessive use of fertilisers also makes the soil less fertile.
 
• Fertilisers have also become a source of water pollution.

questions.question: Crop rotation is a practice to grow _________ on the same field.

options.text: two or more crops in definite row pattern together
a leguminous crop between two cereal crops

questions.solution:
__**Solution**__**:**

 
• Practice in which different types of crops** like leguminous crops and non leguminous crop**s are grown alternately in the same field is called as Crop rotation.

**Advantages of Crop Rotation:**

1. Improves the fertility of soil by replenishing it with nitrogen .

2. Increases the production of food grains.

3. Saves lots of nitrogen fertilizers as leguminous plants can fix atmospheric nitrogen with the help of bacteria

questions.question: Match the following:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **i-b,ii-c,iii-a,iv-d**

__**Explanation:**__

**i) Kharif Crops - b) Paddy and maize**

__
 
• Kharif crops are grown with the onset of monsoon in different parts of India and harvested in September-October. These crops rely on the rainwater and don't require much irrigation.
 
• Paddy (rice) and maize (corn) are prime examples of Kharif crops as they are typically sown at the beginning of the monsoon season and harvested at the end.
 
• Other Kharif crops include soybean, sugarcane, and cotton.

**ii) Rabi Crops - c) Wheat, gram, pea**

 
• Rabi crops are sown at the end of the monsoon or in the winter season and harvested in the spring or early summer. These crops typically need cooler weather to grow.
 
• Wheat, gram (chickpea), and pea are classic examples of Rabi crops. They are sown around October-November and harvested around March-April in South Asia.
 
• These crops generally require irrigation as they grow in the dry season.

**iii) Chemical Fertilisers - a) Urea and super phosphate**

 
• Chemical fertilizers are synthetically manufactured substances that are applied to crops to enhance their growth and productivity by providing them with necessary nutrients.
 
• Urea is a common nitrogen-based fertilizer, and superphosphate is a widely used phosphorus fertilizer. These substances are crucial for the proper growth of crops by supplying essential nutrients that might be lacking in the soil.

**iv) Organic Manure - d) Animal excreta, cow dung urine and plant waste**

 
• Organic manure is made from natural products such as decomposed plants and animal waste. It enriches the soil by adding organic matter and nutrients.
 
• Commonly used organic manures include animal excreta (such as from cows, horses, and poultry), cow dung, urine, and plant waste (such as crop residues and compost). These materials help improve soil structure, increase moisture retention, and supply a wide range of nutrients to the soil, promoting healthy crop growth.

**Conclusion:**__

Therefore, the correct match is

i) Kharif Crops - b) Paddy and maize

ii) Rabi Crops - c) Wheat, gram, pea

iii) Chemical Fertilisers - a) Urea and super phosphate

iv) Organic Manure - d) Animal excreta, cow dung urine and plant waste

questions.question: The process of loosening and folding the soil is called ________.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Option 3**__ i.e __**Ploughing**__.

__
 
• **Sowing**:

 
 
• It is the process of planting seeds in the soil.
 
 
 
• **Weeding**:
 
 
• The process of removal of unwanted plants that grow in between the crops is called weeding.
 
 
 
• **Ploughing**__:
 
 
• **It is the process of turning and breaking down o r loosening the soil.**
 
• Ploughing improves the aeration of the soil.
 
• It is done to bring the nutrients up to the surface of the soil thus making the soil fertile.
